nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is the expression and coping mechanisms for eco-grief poorly understood?
nodes.answer: There is limited understanding of how people express and cope with eco-grief, as highlighted by emerging research on this emotional state.
nodes.paragraph: Background The term eco-anxiety is one of several generic phrases used to describe negative emotional states, such as cognitive dissonance, sadness, and other types of distress that individuals may feel in response to ecological losses, such as those associated with climate change (Cunsolo & Ellis, 2018 ). Other related terms include ecological grief, climate grief (Randall, 2009 ), and solastagia (Albrecht, 2005) ). We choose the term eco-grief, among others, as a broad label for the negative emotions experienced by observers who witness ecological loss (i.e., such loss may result from various impacts, including climate change, development, biodiversity loss, and others). Despite the emergence of a vocabulary to capture such emotions, how people express and cope with eco-grief is poorly understood (Park et al., 2020 ). The emerging research on eco-grief shows that this emotional state differs from other forms of grief and anxiety that are connected to life events (Clayton, 2020 ). It is often described as being overwhelming (the scope of the problem is vast), ongoing (is based on an event that continues to unfold and is getting worse), and unprecedented (we have no historical models for dealing with biodiversity loss and climate changes on this scale) (Kurth & Pihkala, 2022 ; Pihkala, 2020 ).
